    {"name": "is_hardware", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Category indicator; candidate driver of duration."},
    {"name": "duration_category", "causal_role": "outcome", "named_in_query": true, "rationale": "A binned version of the outcome itself, not an explanatory variable."},
    {"name": "priority_avg_duration", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Group-mean of the outcome by priority -- a target-derived aggregate, essentially leakage from the outcome, not a confounder."},
    {"name": "category_avg_duration", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Group-mean of the outcome by category -- outcome-derived aggregate, not a common cause."},
    {"name": "duration_vs_priority_avg", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Deviation of the outcome from its own group mean -- a transformation of the outcome, not a predictor/confounder."},
    {"name": "duration_vs_category_avg", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Outcome deviation from category mean -- derived from the outcome, not a confounder."},
    {"name": "assignee_avg_duration", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Assignee historical average duration could proxy an assignee/skill effect that plausibly influences both assignment (which tickets/priorities go to whom) and duration; however it is largely outcome-derived, weakening its status."},
    {"name": "duration_vs_assignee_avg", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Outcome deviation from assignee mean -- derived from the outcome, not a confounder."},
    {"name": "has_round_duration", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Degenerate flag (all zeros); noise, no causal role."}
  ],
  "treatment_present": true,
  "treatment_columns": ["priority_numeric", "is_network", "is_database", "is_software", "is_hardware"],
  "confounders": [
    {"name": "assignee_avg_duration", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.3}
  ],
  "confounder_quality": 0.15,
  "rationale": "The set supplies candidate treatments (priority, category one-hots) but essentially NO genuine confounders. A confounder must be a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome that is not derived from the outcome. Almost all remaining columns are outcome-derived aggregates or deviations (priority_avg_duration, category_avg_duration, assignee_avg_duration, and the *_vs_*_avg deviations) -- these are transformations of the outcome itself, constituting target leakage rather than confounding adjustment. There are no independent covariates such as ticket complexity, workload/queue length at open time, reassignment count, business hours, caller/requester attributes, or assignment-group capacity that would plausibly cause both which priority/category a ticket gets and how long it takes. Because the system surfaced no true common-cause covariates and instead recycled the outcome into group means, the causal-attribution capability under test is not realised."
}
